staged_source_snapshot.description: Local staged checkout whose line numbers match the saved ASan trace. The sample metadata's vulnerable/fixed commits and staged patch do not explain the crashing source lines.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42504982 (espeak-ng): Stack-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target ssml-fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42504982
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / default_crash_trace.txt / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source in gt_results/arvo_42504982/_work/src/espeak-ng / staged poc / local espeak-ng git history for supporting fix evidence
bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is the exact 6625-byte file `gt_results/arvo_42504982/poc` (sha256 `458e9909c881c018a44c6da9c5d38f6e07aaf7d75e9e9bd29384a2c99a129e96`). `tests/ssml-fuzzer.c` copies those bytes into a NUL-terminated string and calls `espeak_Synth` with `espeakCHARS_UTF8 | espeakPHONEMES | espeakSSML`. On the crashing path, `TranslateClause()` reads one clause into `source`, normalizes it into the stack buffer `sbuf` while maintaining per-word `words[].start` offsets, and selects a clause word pointer as `&sbuf[words[ix].start]`. `TranslateWord3()` receives that base pointer as `word_start`, derives the current translation cursor `wordx`, and calls `TranslateRules()` with that cursor; `TranslateRules()` copies it into scan cursor `p`, and `MatchRule()` uses `pre_ptr = *word` from that current cursor before decrementing `pre_ptr` for the PRE `RULE_LETTERGP2` call to `IsLetterGroup(tr, pre_ptr, letter_group, 1)`. Vulnerable `IsLetterGroup()` computes `w = word - len + 1` from the candidate group-string length `len` without checking that enough bytes remain before the passed-in cursor to walk back to the NUL sentinel at the start of `sbuf`. The next comparison loop dereferences `*w`, and ASan reports the saved stack-buffer-overflow read at `src/libespeak-ng/dictionary.c:714`, with the faulting address three bytes before `TranslateClause`'s `sbuf`. The staged `patch.diff` and metadata `fix_commit` are unrelated changelog-only artifacts, but local espeak-ng history contains the corresponding `IsLetterGroup: Do not blindly walk back in the word` fix (`1ce5a1bb` / `34a12c83`), which replaces the raw subtraction with a bounded walk back to the NUL sentinel.

source.code: terminator = ReadClause(tr, source, charix, &charix_top, N_TR_SOURCE, &tone, voice_change_name);
source.description: Source. `TranslateClause()` invokes the clause parser to materialize the next attacker-controlled clause into the local `source[]` text buffer and `charix[]` map before any dictionary rule matching.
source.value_from: The staged 6625-byte `gt_results/arvo_42504982/poc` witness is copied by `tests/ssml-fuzzer.c:61-65` into a NUL-terminated string and passed to `espeak_Synth` with `espeakCHARS_UTF8 | espeakPHONEMES | espeakSSML`. `Synthesize()` admits that string at `src/libespeak-ng/speech.c:449`, and this `ReadClause()` call is the first clause-specific project statement that fills the `TranslateClause` buffers consumed by the crashing path.

root_cause.description: Root cause. For PRE letter-group string matches, `IsLetterGroup()` derives the lookbehind pointer by subtracting `len - 1` bytes from the caller-supplied cursor `word` without checking whether that cursor can walk back to the left-boundary NUL sentinel of `sbuf`.
root_cause.note: Local history commits `1ce5a1bb` / `34a12c83` replace this subtraction with a bounded byte-by-byte walk that aborts when the NUL sentinel is reached. The staged `patch.diff` itself is unrelated changelog text.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. The comparison loop dereferences `*w` after step 14 has underflowed the lookbehind pointer derived from the current rule-matching cursor.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 1` at `src/libespeak-ng/dictionary.c:714:17` and places `TranslateClause`'s `sbuf` at [5632, 6432), with the faulting address at offset 5629, three bytes before the buffer.

tainted_value_origin.description: This is where the normalized clause buffer and the final recorded `words[ix].start` offset yield the base pointer for the currently selected word. That pointer later enters `TranslateWord3()` as `word_start`; the saved artifacts do not reveal whether the crashing cursor stayed here or advanced within the same `sbuf` word before `TranslateRules()`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: `TranslateClause()` seeds `sbuf` with a leading NUL sentinel, writes the normalized clause text into it, adjusts `words[word_count].start` when inserted spaces shift a word start (`translate.c:2297`, `2391`, `2445`, `2494`), records each next word start with `words[word_count].start = ix` at `translate.c:2499`, and then selects the current word from that buffer for downstream translation.

parser_admitted.description: The attacker-controlled witness is admitted into the project text decoder here. On the synchronous path, `Synthesize()` then immediately enters `SpeakNextClause(0)` and `TranslateClause()`.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false, so Stage 02 did not add instrumentation. The chain is closed from the staged source, saved ASan traces, `reproduction_report.json`, and the local repository history only.

The staged metadata patch is not a real fix for this crash: `patch.diff` and `fix_commit` `65cccab7420ae67178bfe710fee727d21581200a` only update `CHANGELOG.md`. The actual missing bound check is supported instead by local historical fixes `1ce5a1bb` / `34a12c83` in `src/libespeak-ng/dictionary.c`.

The saved runtime artifacts do not expose the exact dictionary group bytes or the exact runtime offsets of `wordx` and `p` inside the selected word. The trace therefore models the proven source-level cursor chain `word -> word_start -> wordx -> p_start -> p -> pre_ptr` and relies on the ASan frame at `MatchRule` PRE `RULE_LETTERGP2` plus the faulting address three bytes before `sbuf` to close the underflow, without claiming the crashing cursor was the clause-initial `&sbuf[3]`.

coarse_trace.summary: The fuzzer-supplied UTF-8/SSML witness is admitted to the text decoder and `TranslateClause()` materializes the next clause into its local `source` buffer.

`TranslateClause()` normalizes the clause into stack buffer `sbuf`, maintains per-word `words[].start` offsets, selects the current word, and `TranslateWord3()` turns that base pointer into the current cursor `wordx` used for rule translation.
`TranslateRules()` copies `wordx` into scan cursor `p`, and `MatchRule()` uses that current cursor for PRE `RULE_LETTERGP2` lookbehind before calling `IsLetterGroup(..., pre = 1)`.

Vulnerable `IsLetterGroup()` subtracts the candidate group length from the decremented PRE cursor without a bound check and then dereferences the resulting out-of-bounds lookbehind pointer, producing the saved ASan stack-buffer-overflow read.

fine_trace.code: terminator = ReadClause(tr, source, charix, &charix_top, N_TR_SOURCE, &tone, voice_change_name);
fine_trace.note: Source. `TranslateClause()` asks `ReadClause()` to pull the next attacker-controlled clause from the text decoder into the local `source[]` buffer. The later `sbuf` contents, word boundaries, and rule lookbehind all derive from this clause text.

Before clause words are processed, `TranslateClause()` seeds the stack scratch buffer with a leading NUL sentinel and two spaces and initializes the first `words[]` entry. Later selected words and lookbehind cursors all point into this `sbuf` region, whose left boundary is `sbuf[0]`.

The normalization loop appends attacker-derived output characters into `sbuf` and inserts spaces when words are terminated. This builds the in-buffer word slices that later translation cursors walk over.

As normalization inserts extra spaces before the current word, `words[word_count].start++` shifts that word's recorded start; this contiguous pre-pause path does so, and the same adjustment also occurs at `translate.c:2297`, `2391`, and `2445`. When a word ends, `word_count++; words[word_count].start = ix;` records the next `sbuf` offset, so `words[]` carries the final start index later selected at step 5.

For each selected clause word, `TranslateClause()` uses the final recorded `words[ix].start` offset to alias the corresponding slice of `sbuf` as `word` and passes that base pointer down through `TranslateWord2()`/`TranslateWord()` into `TranslateWord3()` as `word_start`.

`TranslateWord3()` receives the selected `sbuf` slice as `word_start`, optionally skips a leading space inserted by earlier rewrites, and initializes `wordx` as the current cursor it will hand to dictionary rules.

fine_trace.code: wordx += TranslateLetter(tr, wordx, unpron_phonemes, non_initial, current_alphabet);
fine_trace.note: Inside the unpronounceable-prefix loop (`translate.c:765-789`), this is the only statement that can advance `wordx` before rule translation. The saved artifacts do not expose the loop count, so the crashing cursor may be the initial `wordx` from step 6 or a later byte in the same `sbuf` word.

fine_trace.code: end_type = TranslateRules(tr, wordx, phonemes, N_WORD_PHONEMES, end_phonemes, wflags, dictionary_flags);
fine_trace.note: Because the crash stack reaches `TranslateRules()`, the `found == false && *wordx != ' '` remainder path executed and passed the current cursor `wordx` into dictionary rule matching. The callee sees this value as `p_start`, not necessarily the original `word_start` from step 5.
`TranslateRules()` copies its `p_start` argument into the mutable scan cursor `p` before entering the rule-matching loop.

fine_trace.code: MatchRule(tr, &p, p_start, wc_bytes, tr->groups3[ix], &match1, word_flags, dict_flags0);
fine_trace.note: ASan frame #2 points to this `groups3[ix]` call site, so the crashing `MatchRule()` invocation received a pointer to the current scan cursor `p` together with the same `p_start`. The saved artifacts do not expose which loop iteration supplied this cursor.

`MatchRule()` snapshots the current translation cursor with `pre_ptr = *word;`. Because `word` is the caller's `&p`, this PRE lookbehind starts from `TranslateRules()`' current cursor, not from the original word-start pointer selected in `TranslateClause()`.
In the PRE-rule path, `MatchRule()` moves the lookbehind cursor one byte left before testing the preceding context.

fine_trace.code:
letter_group = LetterGroupNo(rule++);
if ((n_bytes = IsLetterGroup(tr, pre_ptr, letter_group, 1)) >= 0) {
fine_trace.note: The crashing path takes the PRE `RULE_LETTERGP2` arm and passes that decremented cursor into `IsLetterGroup(..., pre = 1)`.

Root cause. For PRE string groups, `IsLetterGroup()` measures the candidate group text with `strlen(p)` and sets `w = word - len + 1` with no check that the caller-supplied cursor can walk back `len - 1` bytes before crossing the NUL sentinel at the start of `sbuf`. Local history commits `1ce5a1bb` / `34a12c83` fix this by walking back one byte at a time and aborting when the sentinel is reached.

Sink. The comparison loop dereferences `*w` after step 14 has underflowed it. The saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 1` at this line and shows `TranslateClause`'s `sbuf` occupying [5632, 6432), with the faulting address at offset 5629, three bytes before the buffer.

poc.trigger: Run the staged `poc` with the saved `ssml-fuzzer` harness; AddressSanitizer reproduces a stack-buffer-overflow READ in `IsLetterGroup`.
